free_tier.stated: No free tier is listed. For every full or partial hour when an accelerator runs in your account, you are charged $0.025 until it is deleted.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a tunnel or an address, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: a live tunnel, not stored bytes

egress.terms: USD 0.025 per accelerator-hour plus DT-Premium per GB on top of standard Data Transfer rates; DT-Premium is USD 0.015/GB from United States & Canada or Europe & Israel to United States, Mexico, Canada or Europe edge locations; no byte cap is stated on the page

interface_detail: accelerators, listeners, endpoint groups and endpoints, created through the console, CLI or API
tooling: AWS console, CLI or API; an NLB or EC2 instance as the endpoint
chaining: only with an AWS origin, so it does not chain with a free VM from another cloud

limits.value: DT-Premium from United States & Canada is $0.015/GB to United States, Mexico, Canada and Europe edge locations and up to $0.105/GB to others, on top of standard Data Transfer rates
USD 0.025 per accelerator-hour for each provisioned accelerator, enabled or disabled

binding_note: No byte cap is stated: cost is linear in GB, a fixed USD 0.025 per accelerator-hour plus DT-Premium per GB, on top of standard Data Transfer rates. The endpoint must be an AWS resource (Network Load Balancer, Application Load Balancer, EC2 instance or Elastic IP address).

identity_cost.detail: An AWS account with a payment method; there is no free-tier accelerator.

reliability_note: TCP fragments are dropped at the edge because the AWS network does not support them; UDP fragments are forwarded
confidence_note: Anycast, UDP fragment forwarding, the endpoint types and the two rates are quoted from pages read today. A measured claim would need an accelerator created and a UDP listener counted.

evidence.proved: The static IP addresses are anycast from the AWS edge network. Global Accelerator forwards UDP fragments to the configured endpoint, which reassembles the original IP packet.
Endpoints for standard accelerators can be Network Load Balancers, Application Load Balancers, Amazon EC2 instances, or Elastic IP addresses
We are charged $0.025 per accelerator-hour, and DT-Premium is $0.015/GB for the first 10 TB from United States & Canada and Europe
every provisioned accelerator, enabled or disabled, pays a fixed hourly fee plus DT-Premium on top of standard Data Transfer rates
evidence.quote: For every accelerator that is provisioned (both enabled and disabled), you are charged a fixed hourly fee and an incremental charge over your standard Data Transfer rates

evidence.proved: DT-Premium per GB by destination for a United States & Canada source

evidence.quote: Endpoints for standard accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator can be Network Load Balancers, Application Load Balancers, Amazon EC2 instances, or Elastic IP addresses.

price_per_tb_month: USD 18 per month plus USD 0.015 per GB
notes: The cleanest documented UDP anycast in the lane and the only one with a published per-GB rate, but the endpoint list is AWS-only, so a free VM on Oracle or GCP cannot be the origin. Compared with Gcore (EUR 17/month flat) it is cheaper at low volume and has no rule model, but it buys reachability into AWS, which the VM already had.

extras.wg_detail: Global Accelerator forwards UDP fragments to the configured endpoint, so a WireGuard listener on an EC2 instance behind it is reachable on the listener port.
extras.volume_stated: Unmetered in the sense that nothing is capped: USD 0.025 per accelerator-hour plus DT-Premium of USD 0.015/GB for the first 10 TB from United States and Canada or Europe. 1 TiB/month is 1,099.5 GB at USD 0.015, about USD 16.49, plus USD 18 of fixed fee.
extras.transit_note: traffic enters the AWS global network at the nearest edge and exits to the endpoint
